# How Guard picks between rules

When more than one rule matches an event, Guard decides which one wins. `hol-guard policy check` shows
you the winner and every rule that lost, with the reason. `hol-guard policy test` reports whether each test
got the effect and rule it expected; run `policy check` on the test's event to see why a rule lost.

## The frozen runtime contract

The text below is quoted from [`semantics.md`](../../spec/guard-policy/v1alpha1/semantics.md), the
normative specification. It is the contract the runtime keeps.

> ## Current runtime precedence (frozen)
>
> This representation release does not change runtime precedence:
>
> 1. An eligible local one-shot approval is atomically claimed first.
> 2. Active persisted rows are ordered by scope: artifact, workspace, publisher, harness, global.
> 3. Within workspace/harness/global, an artifact-constrained row precedes an unconstrained row.
> 4. Remaining ties use `updated_at` descending. Source is not a tie-breaker: a local and remote row at the same specificity follow the same timestamp rule.
> 5. Expired rows do not participate. Integrity-invalid local rows are skipped; a valid next candidate may win.
> 6. A signed Cloud `block` or `review` does not receive absolute priority over a more-specific or newer local `allow`; changing that rule requires a separate safety contract.
>
> The decision fixtures freeze exact-vs-broad, active-vs-expired, once-vs-permanent, and local-vs-remote outcomes. Compilers and representation changes MUST preserve them.

## Reading the explanation

`policy check --format json` lists one candidate per compiled row, in document order. A rule that names
several artifacts compiles to one row per artifact, so one rule id can appear more than once. Each candidate
has a state:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `selected` | This rule decided the event. |
| `outranked` | The rule matched and lost. The reason says why: `block_wins`, `more_specific_rule` or `tie`. |
| `unmatched` | The rule does not apply. The reason names the first field that failed. |
| `expired` | The rule matched but its lifetime had ended at the event time. |
| `not_enforced` | The rule matched but Guard does not enforce it for this kind of artifact. |

When two rules tie on effect and specificity, the decision is flagged `ambiguous` and both rule ids are
listed in `tiedRuleIds`. A test that names an expected rule (`expect.ruleId`) and hits an ambiguous winner
is reported as `ambiguous`, so you can tighten a match until one rule clearly wins. A test that checks only
`expect.effect` passes when the tied rules agree on the effect.

If more than 256 rules match one event, Guard blocks the event without naming a rule and
`matchLimitExceeded` is true.
